bio.jane/contract.noScientificClaim: Relays the remote service's own result unchanged; it computes no number of its own, so the service is the authority for what comes back.
bio.jane/contract.question: What does this authoritative database return for this query?

description: Ask one of the ~60 authoritative databases a question and hand its rows downstream — Ensembl, UniProt, ClinVar, gnomAD, ChEMBL, PubChem, InterPro, STRING, PDB, AlphaFold, the GWAS Catalog, PubMed and the rest. Nothing here computes science: a connector returns what the authority already published, which is the rule that an authoritative registry outranks anything kept locally.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

limit.description: cap on rows returned, where the authority honours one.

query.description: what to ask, in the authority's own terms — an identifier, a gene symbol, or one of its command forms such as `ensembl_lookup:BRCA2`.

name: query_database

authority.description: which authority answered, stated rather than implied

endpoints.description: the URLs actually called — the provenance a methods section needs

envelope.description: the whole response, for a row shape this node's `results` does not name
